sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project manifest and commands
sections.what: Gives the project its name and version, lists the libraries it uses for the website, maps, AI services, database and geographic area, and defines the commands for running, building, checking and testing it.
sections.why: This is the standard place for a Node.js project to declare what it needs and how to run it.
sections.watch_out: Adding or changing a library here changes what gets installed. Keep the version ranges in step with the lock file, if one is used.

summary: Project manifest that names the app, lists its libraries, and defines the commands for running, building, testing and checking it.
purpose: Tells the package manager what to install and gives short commands such as dev, build, test and eval.
why: Every Node.js project needs this file. The scripts give one place for common tasks.
how: The package manager reads the dependencies and installs them. The scripts run the tools with the given names when a user types the matching command.
inputs: The user types commands such as npm run dev or npm test.
outputs: Installed libraries, a built app, test results, and lint or type reports.
risks: Broad version ranges with a caret allow new minor versions to install, which can change behaviour. The packet does not show a lock file that pins exact versions.
debug: If a command fails, check the matching script here first. If an install breaks, compare with the lock file, if one exists in the project.
